tutorial.title: Coding Subclass Properties
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn how to create specific subclasses by adding properties.

lessons.title: Intro
lessons.interactiveContent:
Imagine we're expanding the role-playing game with a character: the warrior. Warriors wear armor and use a war cry when they attack.

Since subclasses can have their own properties, we can easily add these extra features to a character.

lessons.title: Super
lessons.interactiveContent:
First, we need to create a subclass that has the same properties as its superclass. We'll do that by calling the super() method.

Add the super() method to call the constructor of the superclass.

Make sure to pick super.
lessons.hardModeContent:
First, we need to create a subclass that has the same properties as its superclass. We'll do that by calling the super() method.

In the subclass constructor, call the superclass constructor so the inherited weapon property is initialized.

Make sure to pick weapon, followed by super.

lessons.title: Weapons
lessons.interactiveContent:
We want the Warrior class to have the same weapon property as the Human class.

Use super(weapon) to call the Human class's constructor and create the weapon property.

Make sure to pick super followed by ( and then weapon, ).
lessons.hardModeContent:
We want the Warrior class to have the same weapon property as the Human class.

Complete the superclass call that passes the constructor's weapon to the inherited constructor.

Make sure to pick super, followed by (, weapon, and finally ).

lessons.title: Property
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can make the Warrior subclass more specific by adding properties to it. We need to add any extra properties after super().

Add a warCry parameter to the constructor and store it as a property.

Make sure to pick warCry, followed by this.warCry = warCry;.
lessons.hardModeContent:
We can make the Warrior subclass more specific by adding properties to it. We need to add any extra properties after super().

Give the new warrior a personal cry by accepting it in the constructor and saving it on the instance.

Make sure to pick , warCry, followed by super, this.warCry, and finally warCry.

lessons.title: Attack
lessons.interactiveContent:
Now that we have different properties, we can add methods that use these properties.

Add the this.warCry property in the subclass's attack() method to see how the method behaves compared to the superclass.

Make sure to pick this.warCry.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Now that we have different properties, we can add methods that use these properties.

Make attack() print the current warrior's stored cry after the inherited attack.

Make sure to pick super.attack(), followed by this.warCry.

lessons.title: Customized
lessons.interactiveContent:
With the customized attack() method, every new Warrior instance we create can have their own war cry.

Make sure to pick leonidas, followed by "Molon labe!".
lessons.hardModeContent:
With the customized attack() method, every new Warrior instance we create can have their own war cry.

Create Leonidas with "spear" as the weapon and "Molon labe!" as the cry.

Make sure to pick leonidas, followed by new, Warrior, "spear", and finally "Molon labe!".

lessons.title: Question: super constructor
lessons.interactiveContent:
What method do we need to call to create a subclass that has the same properties as it's superclass?

super()constructor()

Make sure to pick super().
lessons.hardModeContent:
A subclass constructor must initialize properties inherited from its parent. Which call does that?

super()constructor()extends()

Make sure to pick super().

lessons.title: Question: Subclass properties
lessons.interactiveContent:
When can we add extra properties to a subclass?

After calling the super() methodAny point in the constructor

After calling the super() method.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A Warrior constructor receives a new warCry property. When can it assign that property?

After calling the super() methodAny point in the constructorBefore the constructor receives its parameters

After calling the super() method.

lessons.title: Question: Use subclass properties
lessons.interactiveContent:
Can a superclass use the properties of a subclass?

NoYes

Make sure to pick No.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A Warrior adds warCry, but Human never defines it. Can a Human method rely on that property?

NoYesOnly after calling super()

Make sure to pick No.

lessons.title: Example: super constructor
lessons.interactiveContent:
Add a call to super to call the Animal class's constructor.

Make sure to pick super followed by ( and then name, ), ;.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Initialize the inherited name property when a Dog is created by calling the parent constructor.

Make sure to pick constructor, followed by super, (, name, and finally ).

lessons.title: Example: Subclass properties
lessons.interactiveContent:
Add a trainer parameter to the constructor and store it as a property.

Make sure to pick , trainer followed by this.trainer and then =, trainer.
lessons.hardModeContent:
In a subclass constructor, call super() before assigning extra properties on this.

Accept a trainer parameter and save it as this.trainer after initializing the inherited name.

Make sure to pick , trainer, followed by super(name), this.trainer, and finally trainer.

lessons.title: Example: Use subclass properties
lessons.interactiveContent:
Use this to access and display the trainer property from the Dog class's speak() method.

Make sure to type this.trainer.

lessons.title: Example: Instantiate subclass
lessons.interactiveContent:
Create an instance of the Dog class and call the speak method.

Make sure to pick = followed by new and then Dog("Lab", "Terry"), rover, .speak().
lessons.hardModeContent:
Store a Dog named "Lab" in rover, then make that instance introduce itself and its trainer.

Make sure to pick Dog, followed by rover, new, "Lab", and finally rover.
